# The numericals7 package {#sec-numericals7}

Every chapter so far has leaned on a small amount of numerical machinery:
finite-difference stencils behind the fallback derivatives of @sec-links and
@sec-distributions7, quadrature behind the expectations of
@sec-transformations, combinatorial enumerations behind the chain rules of
@sec-link-scale, exact higher-order derivatives of recursive maps in
@sec-parameter-families. Before `numericals7` existed each package carried
its own copy of what it needed, and the same set-partition enumeration was
written twice while finite differences existed in three versions. This
chapter presents the package that now holds that machinery once, at the
bottom of the toolkit, where everything above consumes it.

@sec-numerical-jets presents jets, the algebra of truncated Taylor
expansions: a value carried together with every partial derivative to fourth
order, propagated exactly through arithmetic, so that a map written in plain
R differentiates itself. @sec-numerical-stencils presents the single stencil
library -- the weights of a finite-difference rule for any derivative order
at any offsets, from one linear system. @sec-numerical-quadrature presents
quadrature and series summation vectorized over the parameters, which is the
shape a regression model needs: the same integrand at hundreds of parameter
values, evaluated as a matrix rather than in a loop.
@sec-numerical-special presents the special functions the distributions are
written in, each carrying the overflow discipline that was learned on it.
